comparisons.peer_summary: Net revenues increased 16% to $53.51 billion in 2024, driven primarily by higher revenues in Global Banking & Markets (Equities, Investment banking, FICC) and Asset & Wealth Management (Equity investments, Management fees), with slight increases in Platform Solutions.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Goldman Sachs reported revenue growth in their Markets businesses driven by higher Equity Markets activity. Citigroup stated its 2024 revenues increased 6% 'driven by higher Equity Markets and Fixed Income Markets revenues.' Similarly, Goldman Sachs reported net revenues were 16% higher, 'primarily reflecting higher net revenues in Global Banking & Markets,' with the increase in that segment specifically including 'higher net revenues in Equities' and higher Investment banking fees and FICC revenues.

sentences.text: Revenues increased 6%, driven by higher Equity Markets and Fixed Income Markets revenues.
Net revenues were $53.51 billion for 2024, 16% higher than 2023, primarily reflecting higher net revenues in Global Banking & Markets and Asset & Wealth Management.

The increase in net revenues in Global Banking & Markets primarily reflected higher net revenues in Equities, significantly higher Investment banking fees and higher net revenues in Fixed Income, Currency and Commodities (FICC).

comparisons.peer_summary: Principal transactions revenue increased, driven by higher Equity Markets revenue in Prime Finance and Equity Derivatives, partially offset by lower Fixed Income Markets revenue due to declines in macro businesses, which were partially offset by higher revenue in Securitized Products.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclosed specific drivers for their Markets principal transaction revenues, highlighting the interplay between Equity and Fixed Income lines. Citigroup noted overall Markets revenue growth was driven by 'higher Equity Markets and Fixed Income Markets revenues.' In contrast, JPMorgan's principal transactions revenue increased due to 'higher Equity Markets revenue in Prime Finance and Equity Derivatives,' but this was 'predominantly offset by lower Fixed Income Markets revenue.' This shows a divergence where Citi had growth in both equity and fixed income markets, while JPM saw growth in equity offset by declines in fixed income.
